steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a rapid, high-level sketch of how a Transformer works:

1. Input Representation  
  • Tokens → embeddings + positional encodings (so order matters).

2. Self-Attention  
  • For each token you compute three vectors: Query (Q), Key (K), Value (V).  
  • Attention scores = softmax(Q·Kᵀ/√d).  
  • Each token’s new representation = sum of Values weighted by those scores.  
  • “Multi-head” means you do this in parallel with different Q/K/V projections, then concatenate—so the model can attend to different patterns.

3. Feed-Forward & Residuals  
  • After attention, each token vector goes through a small feed-forward network (same one applied to all tokens).  
  • Add & Norm: residual connections + layer normalization keep training stable.

4. Stacking Layers  
  • You stack several attention+FFN blocks. Early layers learn local patterns; deeper layers learn more abstract context.

5. Encoder vs. Decoder (for seq2seq)  
  • Encoder: pure self-attention over inputs.  
  • Decoder: masked self-attention (no peeking ahead) + cross-attention over encoder outputs.

6. Output & Training  
  • Final vectors → linear layer + softmax to predict next token (or classification label).  
  • Trained end-to-end on large text corpora via next-token prediction or similar losses.

Conceptually, it replaces recurrence with attention, letting every token directly interact with every other in each layer—enabling massively parallel training and flexible context modeling.
